front: Options walkthrough: the median week as an income statement?
back: Edge +$13.2k, theta +$46.6k, gamma -$36.4k, vega +$3.4k, other Greeks -$1.6k, hedge residual +$1.3k, hedging costs -$1.4k; total +$25.0k (synthetic). (03-algorithms/h-end-to-end-walkthroughs/walkthrough-options-market-maker.md)

front: Options walkthrough: band versus clock hedging?
back: Hourly hedging left a weekly residual sd of $9.4k; hedging on fills with a band left $1.5k (synthetic). (03-algorithms/h-end-to-end-walkthroughs/walkthrough-options-market-maker.md)

front: Options walkthrough: how is model error paid for?
back: Through selection: theo was 0.33 vol points off when fills arrived, costing 40% of the intended edge (synthetic). (03-algorithms/h-end-to-end-walkthroughs/walkthrough-options-market-maker.md)

front: Execution walkthrough: expected cost and risk of a $500M buy over five even days?
back: Half a day's volume in a $1B-ADV stock: about 46-47 bps ($2.3M) expected cost, but a 254 bps ($12.7M) standard deviation, five times larger. (03-algorithms/h-end-to-end-walkthroughs/walkthrough-institutional-execution.md)

front: Execution walkthrough: the Almgren-Chriss schedule at lambda = 1e-8?
back: Buys 37% on day 1; costs 5.3 bps ($263K) more than even days and cuts the standard deviation by $2.9M. Faster schedules break a 25% participation cap. (03-algorithms/h-end-to-end-walkthroughs/walkthrough-institutional-execution.md)

front: Execution walkthrough: the 75th-percentile week versus benchmarks?
back: 178.8 bps ($8.9M) against the decision price, 132 bps of it timing; the same fills "beat" VWAP by 43 bps and the close by 131 bps. (03-algorithms/h-end-to-end-walkthroughs/walkthrough-institutional-execution.md)

front: What are the two main pipes a US stock order travels?
back: Retail marketable orders mostly go from the broker to a handful of wholesalers that fill them off-exchange. Institutional orders go to an execution algo whose router slices them across 18 exchanges, 33 ATSs and the close. (01-market-structure/life-of-a-stock-order.md)

front: After a US stock trade, who clears and settles it, and when?
back: It prints to the tape (exchange or FINRA TRF); NSCC becomes central counterparty and nets it; DTC settles it one business day later (T+1). (01-market-structure/life-of-a-stock-order.md)

front: Number: one-way latency from a colocated router to an exchange, versus between New Jersey data centers?
back: About 5-50 microseconds colocated; about 90-190 microseconds between Mahwah, Carteret and Secaucus by microwave [Estimate]. A retail app to broker takes 10-100 ms. (01-market-structure/life-of-a-stock-order.md)

front: Define price-time priority, and what loses your place.
back: Better price first, then earlier arrival (FIFO) within a price. Reducing size usually keeps your place; changing price or increasing size sends you to the back. (01-market-structure/the-limit-order-book.md)

front: Why is being early in the queue worth money?
back: Front orders fill more often and on ordinary flow; back orders fill mainly when an informed sweep clears the level, so they are more adversely selected. Worth about half a cent a share in large-tick names [Lore]. (01-market-structure/the-limit-order-book.md)

front: Number: a 1,000-share market buy walks a book with 400 at 100.01, 500 at 100.02, 300 at 100.03. Average price?
back: 100.017 (400 at .01, 500 at .02, 100 at .03): 1.2 cents or about 1.2 bps above the 100.005 mid, $12 on a $100k order (illustrative). (01-market-structure/the-limit-order-book.md)

front: Hidden and iceberg orders: what do they trade away?
back: Visibility for priority: they hide size but queue behind displayed orders at the same price; each iceberg refill usually gets a new timestamp. (01-market-structure/the-limit-order-book.md)

front: Depth versus resilience?
back: Depth: how much you can trade within k ticks of the mid. Resilience: how fast spread and depth recover after a sweep. Impact splits into transient (refill) and permanent (information). (01-market-structure/the-limit-order-book.md)

front: What does an intermarket sweep order (ISO) let a router do?
back: Hit several venues at once without waiting for each venue's order-protection checks; the sender takes responsibility for clearing better-priced protected quotes. (01-market-structure/order-types-and-auctions.md)

front: What do post-only and midpoint-peg orders buy, and at what risk?
back: Post-only guarantees you are the maker (rebate, not fee). Midpoint pegs buy price improvement at the risk of being picked off when the NBBO goes stale. (01-market-structure/order-types-and-auctions.md)

front: Closing auction timeline on NYSE and Nasdaq?
back: New MOC/LOC orders stop at 3:50 p.m. (NYSE) and 3:55 p.m. (Nasdaq); imbalance messages then invite offsetting liquidity until the 4:00 p.m. uncross. (01-market-structure/order-types-and-auctions.md)

front: Number: closing-auction share of US volume over time?
back: About 3% of dollar volume in 2010; a record 9.44% of notional in Q2 2024; about 20% on index-rebalance and expiry days. (01-market-structure/order-types-and-auctions.md)

front: Number: US venue landscape and off-exchange share?
back: 18 exchanges (Oct 2026), 33 NMS-stock ATSs, 200+ other off-exchange dealers. Off-exchange was 50.6% of 2025 volume, the first annual majority; about four-fifths went through principal dealers. (01-market-structure/venues-and-retail-flow.md)

front: Why do wholesalers pay for retail order flow?
back: Retail flow is less toxic: it rarely predicts the next price move, so wholesalers can give price improvement, pay PFOF and still earn a spread. (01-market-structure/venues-and-retail-flow.md)

front: Number: a wholesaler's illustrative per-share P&L on a retail sell at $50.006 (mid $50.00)?
back: +0.60 cents spread captured, -0.10 adverse selection, -0.15 PFOF, -0.10 hedging, fees, clearing and tech: net +0.25 cents a share (illustrative). (01-market-structure/venues-and-retail-flow.md)

front: Status of the SEC's four December 2022 equity proposals (as of 2026-11)?
back: Two adopted (Rule 605 disclosure; ticks, access fees and round lots); two withdrawn on 2025-06-12 (Order Competition Rule and Regulation Best Execution). (01-market-structure/venues-and-retail-flow.md)

front: Define the NBBO.
back: The best displayed round-lot bid and offer across all exchanges, computed centrally by the SIPs; serious traders also compute it themselves from direct feeds. (01-market-structure/nbbo-and-market-data.md)

front: Number: how far behind direct feeds is the SIP, and why?
back: Roughly 0.2-0.5 ms for a colocated reader [Estimate], mostly geography and an extra hop, not slow processing. That gap is the raw material of latency arbitrage. (01-market-structure/nbbo-and-market-data.md)

front: SIP versus direct feeds: content?
back: The SIP carries top of book per exchange, NBBO, trades, LULD bands and (from 2026) best odd-lot quote. Direct feeds carry full depth, often order by order, needed to track queue position. (01-market-structure/nbbo-and-market-data.md)

front: Number: maker-taker fees at the top tier?
back: Makers earn up to about 0.29 cents a share (Nasdaq top rebates $0.0029-0.00295); takers pay up to the $0.0030 cap. Inverted venues reverse the signs. (01-market-structure/fees-rebates-and-ticks.md)

front: Spot the error: "Rule 612 bans sub-penny executions in stocks above $1."
back: Rule 612 bans sub-penny quotes (displaying, ranking or accepting orders), not executions. Midpoint pegs fill at half-pennies and wholesalers give fractions of a cent of improvement. (01-market-structure/fees-rebates-and-ticks.md)

front: Define a tick-constrained stock and what competition moves to.
back: One where the spread market makers would quote is narrower than one tick, so it is pinned at a tick. Competition moves to queue position, fee schedules and speed. (01-market-structure/fees-rebates-and-ticks.md)

front: Price-tiered round lots since 2025-11-03?
back: 100 shares up to $250; 40 shares at $250.01-1,000; 10 shares at $1,000.01-10,000; 1 share above $10,000, by prior-month average closing price. (01-market-structure/fees-rebates-and-ticks.md)

front: Number: how much of a market maker's gross revenue is the rebate in the fees-page example?
back: 37% of $0.0079 gross per share; without it the book loses $0.0013 a share. Under the 2024 rules the illustrative net goes from +$0.0016 to -$0.0006. (01-market-structure/fees-rebates-and-ticks.md)

front: Number: value of switching one share from taking to making?
back: About 0.6 cents (from -0.30 to +0.29 cents); for a book trading 5M shares a day, about $30,000 a day or $7.5M a year (illustrative), before selection and non-fill costs. (01-market-structure/fees-rebates-and-ticks.md)

front: Formula: fair value of an index future?
back: Spot times carry, F = S e^((r - q)T): financing minus dividends. Example: S 6,000, r 4.30%, q 1.30%, T 0.25 gives 6,045.2 (illustrative). (01-market-structure/etf-futures-options-linkages.md)

front: What sets the ETF no-arbitrage band?
back: The cost of trading the basket plus creation fees; authorized participants create and redeem in kind when the ETF strays outside it. (01-market-structure/etf-futures-options-linkages.md)

front: Is 0DTE hedging amplifying or dampening intraday moves?
back: Contested: one study links higher 0DTE volume to about 14% higher daily S&P 500 volatility; others find dealer gamma goes with lower intraday realized volatility. (01-market-structure/etf-futures-options-linkages.md)

front: The three requirements of a short sale?
back: A locate before the order (Reg SHO Rule 203), a lender at a floating fee, and recall risk for as long as the position is open. (01-market-structure/shorting-financing-and-settlement.md)

front: Number: typical borrow-fee buckets?
back: General collateral about 0.25-0.50% a year; warm 0.5-5%; hard-to-borrow 5-50%+, occasionally triple digits [Lore]. (01-market-structure/shorting-financing-and-settlement.md)

front: Rules 201 and 204 in one line each?
back: Rule 201: after a 10% drop, shorts may only be priced above the national best bid for the rest of that day and the next. Rule 204: fails from short sales must close out by the open of T+2. (01-market-structure/shorting-financing-and-settlement.md)

front: Number: financing and borrow drag on a long-short book in the shorting example?
back: $7.35M a year, 2.9% of capital: $2.0M long financing, $1.35M GC borrow, $4.0M on the 10% of shorts that are hard to borrow; about 29% of 10% gross alpha (illustrative). (01-market-structure/shorting-financing-and-settlement.md)

front: Live versus deferred market-structure rules (as of 2026-11)?
back: Live: price-tiered round lots, odd-lot best quote on the SIP, amended Rule 605, T+1. Deferred: half-penny tick and 10-mil fee cap (Nov 2027), Form SHO and lending reporting (2028-2029). (01-market-structure/recent-changes.md)

front: What overnight trading change is coming, and when?
back: 23-hour weekday stock trading on Nasdaq, NYSE Arca and the SIPs, targeted for 2026-12-06 (not live as of 2026-11). (01-market-structure/recent-changes.md)

front: Name the seven businesses that share the quant toolkit in US equities.
back: Electronic market makers, HFT prop shops, quant hedge funds, multi-manager quant pods, systematic factor managers, CTAs and agency execution desks. (00-start-here/the-big-picture.md)

front: Which two coordinates place any quant business, and what do they predict?
back: Holding horizon and edge source. They predict capital source, capacity, Sharpe ratio and how the strategy dies. (00-start-here/the-big-picture.md)

front: The pipeline in one line?
back: Data, signals, forecast, portfolio, orders, fills, P&L, then feedback to signals: closed in microseconds by a market maker and monthly by a factor manager. (00-start-here/one-page-cheat-sheet.md)

front: Three questions to ask of any Sharpe ratio?
back: Gross or net? Over what period? Backtest or live? (00-start-here/one-page-cheat-sheet.md)

front: Spot the error: "Market neutral means dollar neutral."
back: A quant means beta-neutral and factor-neutral too; dollar-neutral books can hide factor bets. (00-start-here/one-page-cheat-sheet.md)

front: Spot the error: "Front-running means trading ahead of predictable index flows."
back: Front-running is trading ahead of a known client order (FINRA Rule 5270 covers imminent blocks). Trading announced index changes is not front-running. (00-start-here/one-page-cheat-sheet.md)

front: What are the three learning paths?
back: A 90-minute sprint (7 pages), the 4-hour Core Path (14 pages, about 85% from modules 02-03) and a 2-week Deep Path (all of 02 and 03 with labs, then support modules, quizzes and flashcards). (00-start-here/learning-paths.md)

front: Glossary: bid-ask bounce?
back: Spurious negative autocorrelation in trade-price returns from trades alternating between bid and ask (Roll 1984). Reversal backtests on last-trade prices harvest it on paper; use midquotes, lag a bar and charge the spread. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: effective versus realized spread?
back: Effective: 2q(P - M) against the arrival mid, the cost actually paid. Realized: 2q(P - M at t + h), what the liquidity provider kept. The difference is price impact (adverse selection). (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: Fama-MacBeth regression?
back: Run a cross-sectional regression each period, then average the slopes and use their time-series standard error. Each period's slope is also a characteristic-mimicking portfolio's return. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: frequent batch auction?
back: Budish, Cramton and Shim's (2015) design: uniform-price sealed-bid auctions every fraction of a second, so speed edges smaller than the interval stop winning. Not adopted in US equities. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: speed bump?
back: A deliberate delay on incoming orders, e.g. IEX's 350-microsecond coiled fiber, letting the venue reprice pegged orders before latency arbitrageurs pick them off. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: kill switch?
back: A control that immediately cancels a firm's or strategy's open orders and blocks new ones when a limit is breached (position, loss, message rate, position mismatch). (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: locate, and who is exempt?
back: The Reg SHO Rule 203(b)(1) requirement that a broker have reasonable grounds to believe shares can be borrowed before a short sale. Bona fide market making is excepted. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: odd lot, and its SIP status?
back: An order or trade below a round lot; around half or more of trades by count, yet not setting the NBBO. The SIPs show a best odd-lot quote since late April 2026; depth deferred to May 2028. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: conditional order?
back: A dark-pool indication that rests non-binding; on a potential match the sender is invited to firm up within a short window. Venues penalize low firm-up rates. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: information leakage?
back: Others inferring a large order from its footprint (child patterns, venue choices, pings, firm-ups) and trading ahead. TCA sees it as adverse drift beyond the impact model. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: gamma scalping?
back: Holding long options and repeatedly delta-hedging, which sells after rises and buys after falls; profits when realized volatility exceeds the implied volatility paid. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: fill probability, and why it is modeled with markouts?
back: The probability a passive order executes within a horizon, given queue position, arrivals, cancels and price moves. Fills that happen are adversely selected relative to those that do not. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: spoofing?
back: Placing orders intending to cancel them, to fake supply or demand and move price toward genuine orders; layering is the multi-level variant. Surveillance checks order-to-trade ratios and cancel timing. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: trade-through rule, and its status?
back: Reg NMS Rule 611: no executions at prices worse than a protected quote displayed elsewhere; ISOs are the exception. The SEC proposed repealing it on 2026-06-11. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: s-score?
back: Standardized distance of a stock's cumulative factor residual from equilibrium, s = (X - m) / sigma_eq (Avellaneda and Lee 2010): open beyond about 1.25, close inside about 0.5-0.75. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: basis, and fair basis for an index future?
back: F - S. Fair basis is the net carry, roughly S(e^((r - q)T) - 1) for financing r and dividend yield q. Index arbitrageurs trade deviations net of costs. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: survivorship bias?
back: Overstating backtests by using only securities that still exist. Fix: a point-in-time universe with delisted names and delisting returns; matters most for small-cap, value and distress signals. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: breadth, and why it is usually overstated?
back: The number of independent bets a year in the Fundamental Law. Correlated bets (500 stocks loading on one sector, a slow signal rebalanced daily) are not independent. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary formula: half-life of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck or AR(1) spread?
back: ln 2 / kappa for OU speed kappa; -ln 2 / ln b periods for an AR(1) with coefficient b. Used to filter spreads and set holding periods. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: designated market maker (DMM)?
back: NYSE's successor to the specialist: assigned per stock, obliged to quote and run the open, close and reopenings, in return for parity allocations and fee benefits. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: rank IC versus Pearson IC?
back: Rank IC is the Spearman correlation of signal and later returns, robust to outliers and scale. A large gap to Pearson IC usually means a few extreme names drive the result. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: Glossary: walk-forward analysis and its weakness?
back: Fit on a window, test on the next unseen period, roll forward. It mimics live use but yields one path and still overfits if many variants are tried. (09-reference/glossary.md)

front: What separates the seven kinds of quant firm, given that their math overlaps?
back: Whose capital is at risk and how the decision-makers get paid. (04-industry-and-firms/taxonomy-of-quant-firms.md)

front: What limits own-capital firms versus fee-earning funds?
back: Own-capital firms (market makers, HFT prop) are limited by volume and speed, not money, so rarely take outside investors. Fee funds are limited by market impact, making capacity a manager-investor negotiation. (04-industry-and-firms/taxonomy-of-quant-firms.md)

front: Number: non-bank liquidity providers' 2025 trading revenue versus hedge fund capital?
back: About $114B of trading revenue for non-bank liquidity providers; hedge funds managed about $5.15T (both [Reported]). Liquidity businesses earn large revenue on little capital. (04-industry-and-firms/economics-and-revenue-pools.md)

front: Why is a market maker's revenue a function of volatility and volume? Give Virtu's numbers.
back: Spread capture scales with traded volume and wider volatile-market spreads: Virtu's adjusted net trading income was $3.9M a day in 2019 and $9.0M a day in 2020 [Verified]. (04-industry-and-firms/economics-and-revenue-pools.md)

front: The three economic models of quant firms?
back: Prop (owners keep the P&L and pay staff from a pool), fee funds (manager revenue grows with assets even as returns shrink) and pass-through pods (investors pay platform costs before the performance fee). (04-industry-and-firms/economics-and-revenue-pools.md)

front: The five core quant roles, and the quickest way to place someone?
back: Quant researcher, quant trader, quant developer, software engineer and portfolio manager (owns capital and a P&L). Ask who owns the P&L they work on. (04-industry-and-firms/roles-teams-and-careers.md)

front: Which moats in electronic market making are durable?
back: Flow data, retail and exchange franchises, balance sheet and risk systems; speed is table stakes. Moats compound: more flow, more fill data, better prices, more flow. (04-industry-and-firms/competitive-dynamics-and-ma.md)

front: What do acquirers of trading firms actually buy, and when does consolidation happen?
back: Flow, franchises and client lists, not algorithms. Consolidation follows the volatility cycle: quiet years pushed sales such as GETCO-Knight (2013) and Virtu-KCG (2017). (04-industry-and-firms/competitive-dynamics-and-ma.md)

front: How should you value a market maker?
back: On through-the-cycle revenue per day against volatility and volume, then operating leverage. Citadel Securities' 2022 funding round implied about 3x trailing revenue [Estimate]. (04-industry-and-firms/competitive-dynamics-and-ma.md)

front: Citadel Securities in two facts?
back: The largest US retail wholesaler (claims about 35% of US-listed retail volume) and the largest NYSE designated market maker; separate from Citadel the hedge fund; about $12B 2025 trading revenue [Reported]. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/citadel-securities.md)

front: Why is Virtu the reference case for market-maker economics?
back: It is the one large US electronic market maker with public, audited accounts: FY2025 adjusted net trading income $2,145M, of which Market Making $1,666M [Reported]. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/virtu-financial.md)

front: Jane Street: reported 2025 revenue and a technology fact?
back: About $39.6B of net trading revenue, helped by private-stake gains [Reported]; it writes its software primarily in OCaml. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/jane-street.md)

front: Optiver: what does it publish for 2025?
back: Net trading income EUR 4.556B (+30%) and net profit EUR 1.769B, with 2,233 full-time staff [Verified]; an Amsterdam market maker in listed derivatives, cash equities, ETFs, bonds and FX. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/optiver.md)

front: IMC: core business and 2025 results?
back: Options market making (it calls itself a top-3 global listed-options liquidity provider); 2025 net trading revenue $3,120M (+40%), net profit $968M [Verified]; lead market maker in 150+ US ETFs. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/imc.md)

front: Hudson River Trading: origins and scale?
back: Founded 2002 by computer-science and math graduates, starting in US equities; now multi-asset with 1,000+ staff. Reported 2025 revenue about $12.3B, in line with Citadel Securities [Reported]. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/hudson-river-trading.md)

front: Susquehanna (SIG): core business?
back: Options: it calls itself one of the largest options market participants globally; it also makes ETF markets and wholesales US equities. Private, no financials disclosed; 3,500+ staff. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/susquehanna-sig.md)

front: Jump Trading: what is distinctive about its infrastructure and recent record?
back: Heavy infrastructure: three research data centers, 100+ colocated sites, custom ASIC and FPGA hardware. A subsidiary paid $123M to settle SEC TerraUSD charges in 2024. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/jump-trading.md)

front: Tower Research Capital: structure and the 2019 case?
back: A "team of teams": dozens of independent pods on one shared platform. In 2019 it paid a then-record $67.4M to settle CFTC spoofing charges over former traders' 2012-2013 conduct. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/tower-research-capital.md)

front: D. E. Shaw: how is capital allocated?
back: A 1988 stat-arb pioneer, now multi-strategy (systematic and discretionary); one central Risk Committee allocates capital across units rather than a pod marketplace. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/de-shaw.md)

front: Man Group: its two quant engines?
back: Man AHL (futures trend and multi-strategy quant) and Man Numeric (systematic stock selection); AUM $270.9B at 30 Sep 2026. Systematic long-only equity is now far larger than trend. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/man-group.md)

front: Cubist: where does it sit between pod shop and single-model fund?
back: Point72's quant arm is a hybrid: dozens of independent systematic teams plus a central research group; roughly a sixth of Point72's capital in 2025 by press estimates. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/cubist.md)

front: XTX Markets: what makes its profile unusual?
back: Few people, enormous compute: about 300 employees, over 25,000 GPUs and over 1 exabyte of storage; 2025 net revenue GBP 3.93B across three UK entities [Reported]. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/xtx-markets.md)

front: Renaissance's Medallion: what is known and what is not?
back: Reportedly about 66% a year gross and 39% net in 1988-2018 (from a book, not audited). It is capacity-capped and insider-owned; outside-investor funds have ordinary results. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/renaissance-technologies.md)

front: Two Sigma's 2025 SEC case?
back: A $90M SEC penalty after one researcher's unreviewed model changes moved client returns by hundreds of millions. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/two-sigma.md)

front: AQR: style and scale?
back: The best-known systematic factor manager (value, momentum, carry, defensive, trend); about $187B AUM at end-2025 versus a $226B peak in 2018, after the 2018-2020 quant winter [Reported]. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/aqr.md)

front: Millennium: how does it get quant exposure?
back: A multi-manager pod shop with hundreds of teams; quant exposure via in-house systematic pods, a joint venture with WorldQuant, and mandates to outside quant managers. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/millennium.md)

front: High-Flyer: why is it notable for hardware?
back: A Chinese quant fund that built its own GPU clusters (Fire-Flyer; one with 10,000 A100s per a 2024 DeepSeek paper) and incubated DeepSeek in 2023. (04-industry-and-firms/firm-profiles/high-flyer.md)

front: Where are the US equity matching engines, and where are index futures?
back: A New Jersey triangle: NYSE in Mahwah, Nasdaq in Carteret, Cboe in Secaucus. US equity-index futures trade in Aurora, Illinois. (05-infrastructure/colocation-networks-and-the-speed-of-light.md)

front: Number: speed of light in air versus fiber, and Chicago-New Jersey latency?
back: 1 km takes 3.34 microseconds in air or vacuum but about 4.9 in glass fiber. Microwave Chicago-New Jersey is about 4 ms one way versus 6.65 ms for the best fiber. (05-infrastructure/colocation-networks-and-the-speed-of-light.md)

front: Why is the radio race now over microseconds and weather?
back: The best routes sit within a few percent of the physical limit; no new physics is left, so firms fight over the last microseconds and rain fade. (05-infrastructure/colocation-networks-and-the-speed-of-light.md)

front: What is a strategy's decision budget?
back: The time it can spend between seeing information and acting, from tens of nanoseconds (latency arbitrage) to a whole night (daily factor books). It decides which algorithms are allowed. (05-infrastructure/how-infrastructure-constrains-algorithms.md)

front: FPGA versus CPU versus GPU in trading?
back: FPGAs run simple fixed logic in nanoseconds; CPUs run branchy logic in microseconds; GPUs run batched math over milliseconds to days. Hence slow models arm fast triggers. (05-infrastructure/how-infrastructure-constrains-algorithms.md)

front: Why do speed businesses concentrate in a few firms?
back: Infrastructure is a fixed cost that only strategies with enough volume can carry, and rank against rivals matters more than absolute speed. (05-infrastructure/how-infrastructure-constrains-algorithms.md)

front: What crosses the interface between research and production stacks?
back: Research ships parameters and model weights; production ships back logs of every packet, order and fill. The costliest failures sit at this seam. (05-infrastructure/trading-and-research-tech-stacks.md)

front: Which vendors dominate the trading latency silicon niche?
back: FPGAs: AMD (Xilinx) and Altera (51% owned by Silver Lake). NICs: AMD (Solarflare) and NVIDIA (Mellanox). No credible public figure sizes trading silicon as a market. (05-infrastructure/semiconductor-lens.md)

front: The core rule for talking to a quant?
back: Ask about approach, not alpha: how they decide, measure and fail, never what the signal is. Method questions get long answers; fishing for the secret ends conversations. (07-conversation-playbook/how-to-talk-to-a-quant.md)

front: What is shareable and what is off-limits in a quant conversation?
back: Shareable: methods, infrastructure, failure lessons, published research, industry economics. Off-limits: signals, parameters, positions, P&L or capacity by strategy, latency rank, risk limits, counterparty terms. (07-conversation-playbook/how-to-talk-to-a-quant.md)

front: Red flags to listen for when a quant pitches?
back: A Sharpe ratio with no costs, period or capacity attached; "AI" with no method; returns with no losing stretches. (07-conversation-playbook/how-to-talk-to-a-quant.md)

front: Three ways naive questions fail, and the repairs?
back: Fishing for the secret, asserting a myth, asking for one number stripped of conditions. Repairs: ask for the method, ask about the evidence, ask for the conditions (gross or net, period, capacity). (07-conversation-playbook/faux-pas-and-naive-questions.md)

front: Better version of "What's your Sharpe?"
back: "What net Sharpe is realistic for this kind of strategy, and how fast does it fall with size?" (07-conversation-playbook/faux-pas-and-naive-questions.md)

front: Reply to "A 52% hit rate is barely better than a coin flip."
back: Small edges on many independent bets add up: information ratio is about IC x sqrt(breadth). Ask what their IC and breadth are and how much survives costs. (07-conversation-playbook/faux-pas-and-naive-questions.md)

front: Is losing money last month evidence a Sharpe-1 model is broken?
back: No: with annual Sharpe 1 you lose in about 4 months out of 10 (monthly Sharpe 0.29, P(loss) about 39% assuming normal returns) [Estimate]. (07-conversation-playbook/faux-pas-and-naive-questions.md)

front: What do Basic, Informed, Sharp and the lock symbol mean in the question bank?
back: Basic is a safe opener, Informed shows you know the mechanics, Sharp probes a failure they lived through; the lock marks proprietary territory nobody will answer. (07-conversation-playbook/questions-to-ask.md)

front: What to do when a quant declines to answer?
back: Accept it at once and move one level up, to process, structure or published evidence; anchor on public numbers. (07-conversation-playbook/mock-conversations.md)

front: What does each 30-second elevator explanation answer?
back: What it is, who pays for it and how it breaks. The 2-minute version adds the mechanism, one or two sourced numbers and the honest caveat. (07-conversation-playbook/elevator-explanations.md)

front: How do most quant myths go wrong?
back: They take a true mechanism and drop one ingredient: the costs, the number of trials, the tail, the counterparty or the capacity. Ask for the missing ingredient. (08-calibration/myths-vs-reality.md)

front: Why is a t-statistic above 2 not enough for a new factor?
back: The 1.96 hurdle assumes one test; after hundreds of published factors, Harvey, Liu and Zhu (2016) argue for t > 3.0. Overlapping windows inflate t-stats further unless Newey-West corrected. (08-calibration/myths-vs-reality.md)

front: Number: how much can luck produce in a backtest?
back: Five years of daily data pin an annual Sharpe only to about +/-0.45, so the best of 100 zero-skill strategies shows about 1.1 by luck [Estimate]. (08-calibration/myths-vs-reality.md)

front: Spot the error: "Market makers must hold prices up in a crash."
back: Since December 2010 they must quote within 8%, 20% or 30% of the NBBO, which bans stub quotes; nothing obliges them to absorb one-sided selling. (08-calibration/myths-vs-reality.md)

front: Spot the error: "HFT caused the Flash Crash."
back: The trigger was a 75,000-contract (about $4.1B) E-mini sell program at 9% of volume. HFTs traded over 27,000 contracts in 14 seconds, mostly among themselves, for about 200 net. (08-calibration/myths-vs-reality.md)

front: Spot the error: "Cancelling most of your orders is spoofing."
back: Market makers cancel most orders because quotes follow fair value. Spoofing is bidding or offering with intent to cancel before execution: intent, not cancel rate, is the line. (08-calibration/myths-vs-reality.md)

front: Spot the error: "Medallion is right on most of its trades."
back: Reportedly only about 50.75% of trades [Reported] (Zuckerman 2019); breadth and sizing do the rest. (08-calibration/myths-vs-reality.md)

front: Contested debates: where do the camps usually differ?
back: Rarely on the data; on whose cost, which benchmark, which sample and which experiment. The useful question is "which measure are you using?" (08-calibration/contested-debates.md)

front: Name four of the eight contested debates.
back: HFT and market quality; PFOF; factor premia real or data-mined; value dead or cyclical; ML versus linear models; 0DTE and stability; passive investing and prices; batch auctions. (08-calibration/contested-debates.md)

front: The five formulas that do most sanity-checking work?
back: Standard error of Sharpe, the luck hurdle for N trials, the Fundamental Law, breakeven cost and square-root impact. (08-calibration/sanity-checking-claims.md)

front: Sanity check: when is a claimed Sharpe implausible for its horizon?
back: Net Sharpe above 1.5 from a monthly book, or above 1 at $10B+ in factors: the implied IC would be far above what real signals deliver. (08-calibration/sanity-checking-claims.md)

front: Sanity check: which stress periods should a backtest cover?
back: 2007-2009, March 2020 and the 2022 rate shock; a sample that starts after the last crisis is a red flag. (08-calibration/sanity-checking-claims.md)

front: How is risk management at a quant firm structured?
back: As a stack of limits, each assuming the one above has failed: per-order checks, per-name positions, gross and net notional, factor exposures, liquidity, losses, and finally a kill switch. (06-risk-and-regulation/risk-management-at-quant-firms.md)

front: What do most limits on a neutral quant book actually cap?
back: What the strategy did not mean to own: market beta, sectors, styles such as momentum, and crowded names. Illustrative: beta within +/-0.05-0.1, sector net within +/-1-3% of GMV. (06-risk-and-regulation/risk-management-at-quant-firms.md)

front: Why do pod drawdown stops detect skill poorly?
back: In simulations a 5%-style stop fires within a year for about 20% of zero-skill pods but also about 4% of Sharpe-1 pods [Estimate]; it also pushes PMs toward low volatility and tight factor neutrality. (06-risk-and-regulation/risk-management-at-quant-firms.md)

front: Which historical crises do quant stress tests replay?
back: August 2007, May 2010, August 2015, February 2018, March 2020, January 2021 and August 2024, each hitting different books (stat arb, market makers, ETF arbitrage, short vol, levered books, shorts, carry). (06-risk-and-regulation/risk-management-at-quant-firms.md)

front: What should a well-designed kill switch do?
back: Cancel working orders and block new ones, often still allowing risk-reducing orders; granular per trading system, operated by the risk owner, not overridable by the trader (FIA 2024). Fail safe: quotes come down first. (06-risk-and-regulation/risk-management-at-quant-firms.md)

front: Define model risk, and the controls quant firms use.
back: Losses from models that are wrong or misused (SR 11-7). Controls: research review, staged deployment, live monitoring against expected P&L, and code-risk checks such as comparing orders out with fills in. (06-risk-and-regulation/risk-management-at-quant-firms.md)

front: Knight Capital as a code-risk case: what went wrong?
back: New code reached seven of eight servers; a repurposed flag woke dead logic on the eighth. In about 45 minutes: about $3.5B unintended longs, $3.15B shorts, loss over $460M; no orders-versus-fills check. (06-risk-and-regulation/risk-management-at-quant-firms.md)

front: Which handful of US rules decide how strategies are built?
back: Reg NMS (routing, ticks, fees), Reg SHO (cost of the short side), Rule 15c3-5 (risk checks in the order path) and anti-manipulation law (the line between cancelling quotes and spoofing). (06-risk-and-regulation/rules-that-shape-strategies.md)

front: Status of the trade-through rule and the 2024 tick and fee amendments (as of 2026-11)?
back: Rule 611 is in force, with repeal proposed in June 2026. The half-penny tick and 10-mil access-fee cap are delayed to November 2027; tiered round lots are live since 2025-11-03. (06-risk-and-regulation/rules-that-shape-strategies.md)

front: What does enforcement against manipulation turn on, and the range of US cases?
back: Intent and effect, not cancel rates. From Athena's $1M marking-the-close settlement (2014) to JPMorgan's over-$920M spoofing resolution (2020). (06-risk-and-regulation/rules-that-shape-strategies.md)

front: How do EU rules for algorithms differ from US rules?
back: MiFID II regulates algorithms directly: testing, kill functions, market-making agreements, order-to-trade ratios, tick sizes and clock synchronization, in force since 2018. (06-risk-and-regulation/rules-that-shape-strategies.md)

front: What did India's SEBI do in July 2025 regarding Jane Street?
back: It impounded INR 4,843.57 crore from Jane Street entities over alleged expiry-day index-option manipulation, which the firm disputes [Reported]; the case was pending as of 2026-11. (06-risk-and-regulation/rules-that-shape-strategies.md)
